June is read; the day word is illegible, so the 18th is supplied from Frank, Standeserhebungen 2 (1970), seen only as a Google Books snippet. The field for the arms is blank and there is no seal: probably a draft or rejected fair copy.

identification: Hans Trautson, as guardian with Anton von Brandis, grants Martin Wenig (or Rennig) and Bartlme, grandson of Hans Capler, a field at Lienz in fief, Innsbruck, 2 June 1545
note: Regest read on the image. The beneficiary's surname and a few words in the bounds are uncertain, and the ward is unnamed (Christof von Wolkenstein is a lead, not a reading). The catalogue's 1525 should be 1545; no outside record of the grant found.

identification: Konrad Vos (or Vor), Kellner of Tirol for Duke Sigmund, grants Hermann Aichhorn called Francken a house and garden at Meran zu Erbrecht und Baurecht, 22 July 1454
note: Regest read on the image. The issuer's surname, the place in the dating clause and the rent amount are uncertain or illegible. It is a hereditary tenancy, not a legacy; host volume is incunable VIII/D-9 Nr. 143, as for F-b12f; no outside record of the act found.

identification: Jacobus de Voragine, Legenda aurea (bifolium Frg. 217_1 only): end of Martin, Brice, opening of Elizabeth (Graesse caps. 166-168, pp. 750-753) and part of Clement (cap. 170, pp. 783-786); strip Frg. 217_2 not identified
note: Five passages on all four pages of the bifolium Frg. 217_1 were reread on the native images and agree in wording and sequence with Graesse 1850 (pp. 751 and 784 on page images, other pages on OCR) and with Maggioni's text in Corpus Corporum; the November order Martin-Brice-Elizabeth-(Cecilia)-Clement and the rubricated 'De nomine' prologue, with readings absent from Juan Gil de Zamora's reworking, show it is the Legenda aurea itself. A research reader (Claude) collated four passages; an independent research reader read a fifth (canvas 1 right, Clement, region 4620,2980,2080,580) before seeing the comparison and matched it against Graesse p. 784 and Maggioni. Variants are minor (particles, omissions such as 'visu', corruptions such as 'latiorem et affluentiorem'), and the copy often sides with Maggioni against Graesse ('emulus', 'regionum', 'amen', 'eicite'). The identification covers item 217_1 only: the strip Frg. 217_2 is read only in scraps, not identified, and not shown to come from the same book. Lines outside the five passages rest on the first reading.

identification: Jacobus de Voragine, Legenda aurea: All Saints, the four orders of saints (Graesse cap. 162, pp. 723-726); end of All Souls, Four Crowned, Theodore and opening of Martin (caps. 163-166, pp. 738-741)
note: Five passages on all four pages of the bifolium were read on the native images and agree in wording and sequence with Graesse 1850 (pp. 739-740 on page images, other pages on OCR) and with Maggioni's text in Corpus Corporum, in the Legenda aurea's own 1-11 November sequence with its expository All Saints and All Souls chapters. A research reader (Claude) collated Theodore, the confessors and the Turpin story; an independent research reader read the Four Crowned (canvas 0 left, regions 1400,680,2300,540 and 1400,1120,2300,520) before seeing that comparison and matched it against Graesse pp. 739-740 and Maggioni, and matched the abraded apostles page against Graesse OCR. Variants are small: the added 'ut ait turpinus', the year 'cc.lxxvii' for CCLXXXVII, corruptions such as 'at clamantes', and agreements with Maggioni or Graesse's Ed. Pr. against Graesse's text. Other lines rest on the first reading; the later lower-margin lines were not read.

identification: Jacobus de Voragine, Legenda aurea, four bifolia with chapters for Dominic, Donatus, Cyriacus, Laurence, Cosmas and Damian, Michael, Francis, Dionysius, Eustace, All Saints and Martin (Graesse caps. 113-166)
note: Six passages, at least one on each bifolium, agree in wording and chapter structure with Graesse 1850: Cosmas and Damian (pp. 636-637, page images), Michael (OCR), Laurence (p. 489, page image, and Maggioni's text in Corpus Corporum), and the opening of All Saints and Francis's stigmata (OCR). A research reader (Claude) collated Cosmas and Damian, Michael and the opening of Laurence; an independent research reader read the continuation of Laurence on canvas 6 left (regions 1450,1560,2150,640 and 1450,2880,2150,540) before seeing that comparison and matched it against Graesse p. 489 and Maggioni, and added the canvas 5 and canvas 2 passages. The Philip and Decius passage in Laurence is present; 'Nec te moueat ... dispensauit' is transposed before 'Iste phylippus', 'ut ait Sicardus in chronica sua' and 'Vel forte ideo ...' are absent there, and the copy reads 'phylippus iunior uehementer' with Maggioni; with other small variants ('gemini', 'theodora') these are variants within the work, and the redaction is not determined. About half the text rests on the first reading or is unread.

identification: Noted monastic antiphoner, Matins of the Third Sunday of Lent (Oculi): responsories Memento mei (end) to Dixit Joseph (incipit), with the nocturn-III antiphon Cum immundus spiritus
note: One leaf (old foliation LVI) carrying seven chants of Matins of Oculi (Cantus 007144, 007769, 006999, 006479, 002009, 007146, 006476), read on both faces; text runs from the image labelled 01v to 01r. Chants, verses, cues and the rubric 'Ad cc.' agree with the Morimondo antiphoner, BnF NAL 1411, ff. 71v-72v, on its page images; an independent research reader compared R. Iste est frater (canvas 1) word for word with f. 71v-72r. The leaf lacks Morimondo's versicle 'Scapulis suis' before Merito and shares its 'Tollite de frugibus'. The chant order matches Cistercian inventories (Morimondo, Rein, Lubiąż, Salzinnes) and Köln 1161, supporting Cistercian use as an inference only; date and place of origin are not tested.

identification: Noted monastic antiphoner: Ascension Day (end of Matins to Vespers II), the Ascensiontide Gospel antiphons and Benedictus antiphon of the Sunday after Ascension, and the Common of Apostles (Vespers, invitatory, nocturn I)
note: One leaf read on both faces, text order from the image labelled 01v to 01r with one line lost at the trimmed top; chants identified with Cantus IDs. The texts agree on page images with the Zwiefalten antiphoner, BLB Aug. LX, ff. 112r-v and 166v-167r; an independent research reader compared the antiphons Domine si in tempore to Cum venerit (canvas 0) with f. 112v. Differences: the leaf lacks Zwiefalten's hour versicles and three Exaltare responsories, and reads 'ad dextris', 'domino cooperante', 'Cum venerit' and Annuntiaverunt as sixth apostles' antiphon. The Ascension order matches Zwiefalten and A-Wn 1890 and is not Cistercian, a South German monastic placement inferred from chant order only; the Common of Apostles directly after the Sunday after Ascension and the short last line of canvas 1 are unexplained. Date and house of use not tested.

identification: Albertus Magnus, De anima II tract. 3, end of c. 14 to opening of c. 18 (Borgnet vol. 5, pp. 261-265)
note: Both faces agree in wording and sequence with Albert's De anima II.3.14-18 in Borgnet vol. 5, pp. 261-265, including the rubricated chapter numbers and titles xv-xviii. A research reader (Claude) reread 39 lines on the images and collated them with Borgnet's page images; an independent research reader read the upper part of 76v column a blind on the image and found it agreeing with Borgnet p. 263 across the chapter 16/17 boundary. Variants are scribal: an eye-skip omission ('propter exemplarem explanationem dicta sunt'), 'medio' for 'modo', 'per medium' for 'per mentum', 'post de olfactu' for 'postea de auditu'. The rest of the leaf rests on the image-only reading; the Cologne critical edition was not consulted, and date and origin are not assessed.

identification: Philaretus, De pulsibus (Quid differt questions, ten genera, non-naturals) and Theophilus, De urinis (hypostasis prologue and chapters); a third pulse text not identified
note: A bifolium of a medical book carries Philaretus, De pulsibus and Theophilus, De urinis, each agreeing in wording and sequence with the Articella (Lyon, 1519), often in a shorter form (an extra 'pinguis rubea' and 'pinguis nigra', 'sub rubea' for 'subrufa', a missing 'Pulsus spissus' question). A research reader (Claude) collated the Theophilus prologue and the Philaretus questions with the print's page images; an independent research reader read about 18 lines of Theophilus on canvas 1 blind and found sustained agreement with the print's fol. xv page image, and checked two strip passages against its OCR text only. The page labelled 1r left has a separate pulse text whose ages section parallels the ps.-Soranus Peri sfigmon (ed. Rose) and whose definitions differ; it is not identified. The modern Boethius note in the record is wrong; the strip's relation to the upper piece, date and version are not settled.

identification: Zacharias Chrysopolitanus, In unum ex quatuor III.104, on John 7:3-14 and 7:16-24 (PL 186:327-329)
note: Both faces agree in wording and sequence with Zachary's gospel-harmony commentary in PL 186, cols. 327-329, including the Ambrose/Jerome/Augustine excerpt chain on circumcision, whose source names stand in the leaf's margin. A research reader (Claude) collated all four column fragments with the PL page images; an independent research reader read twelve lines of 74v column a blind on the image and found them verbatim in PL col. 327 apart from the Vulgate 'ego'. The Glossa ordinaria and Bede, Alcuin and Haymo were checked and differ where the leaf follows Zachary. Differences from PL are small (word order, 'de deo' for 'ex Deo', 'personam', 'ut scirent'). The face labelled 74v precedes 74r in text order; text under the patches, date and place in the tradition are not examined.

identification: Revers of 1545 by a married couple (names lost) to Stams abbey for goods held in Erb- und Baurecht, sealed by the Pfleger and judge of Imst
note: Lower half of an original counter-letter (Revers) dated 1545 in words; day and month cut away. The tenants acknowledge goods of Stams abbey in Erb- und Baurecht at 1 lb Berner yearly; one acre lies 'in Tarn[...]' (Tarrenz?), while the bounds name a sawmill and the neighbour Martin Teutschman, whom a Stams Revers of 1549 places by the sawmill at Nassereith, so the goods may lie partly at Nassereith. Sealed by '[.]örburger', Pfleger and judge of Imst: Christoph Hörburger, with the court clerk Georg Engelschalk, seals an Imst tenant's Revers in 1555 (Brixen, Domkapitelarchiv, Urk. 2486). Partial because the issuing couple cannot be named (only 'Bernhar[d]' survives). Later reused as the wrapper of a Stams Kelleramt register for 1570 (Hs. 129).

identification: Lehenbrief: Abbot Paul and the convent of Stams grant the Walthauserin, Johann's son and daughter (Johannes and Petronella) and other Stiftsfreie at Tartsch fields and a meadow at Mals in Erblehen; [15]43 (century supplied), place, day and month lost
note: The regest is read on the image: issuer Abbot Paul and the convent of Stams, beneficiaries, grant in Erb- und Baurecht, plots at Mals near St Martin's church, rent of rye and barley to the Zinskasten at Mals and 1 lb Berner; the endorsement names Johannes, Petronella and Wilhalm. Only 'Unnd Im Dreiundvierzigisten Jare' survives of the date (the preserved readings have 'Dreiunddreissigisten'); the century is supplied: only Paul I Käsinger can issue in a forty-third year, and the Stams archive's regests have Abbot Paul granting in 1541 and 1543 and Abbot Simon from April 1544 (Kaisheim history: 1540-1544; Siebmacher's 1542 is contradicted), giving 1543. The host volume, Hs. 119, is titled for 1578. The 'n.' placeholder leaves open original, engrossment or copy; no outside record found.

identification: Enea Silvio Piccolomini: orations Quamvis omnibus (Regensburg 1454; Wolkan III Nr. 291, pp. 542-546) and Constantinopolitana clades (Frankfurt 1454; Müller, Reichstags-Theatrum I, pp. 479-480); De liberorum educatione, grammar section to the opening of the defence of poets (Wolkan II Nr. 40, pp. 129-140)
note: Two paper bifolia in one fifteenth-century hand, taken from the binding of Stams Hs 308 in 1964: bifolium 1 has the Regensburg oration on one leaf and the Frankfurt oration on the other, bifolium 2 has De liberorum educatione from the end of the analogy and derivation section through barbarism and solecism to the opening of the defence of poets. A research reader reread selected lines on all leaves except the right page of canvas 1 and compared them with Wolkan III and Wolkan II on Internet Archive OCR and with Müller 1713 on the MDZ page image (p. 480) and OCR (p. 479). An independent research reader read seven lines of canvas 3 right (box 4350,2180-6650,2620) on the image and found them in agreement with Wolkan II p. 131 on the page image, and checked the locus of canvas 3 at pp. 129, 130, 138 and 140. Variants are minor (e.g. vitanda? / vindicanda, nostro / vestro, Viscella / vistula, omission of nobilissimum Ladislaum, dicemus / dicamus). The right page of canvas 1 and most of the left pages of canvases 2 and 3 rest on the image-only first reading, which was exposed to a pencil note naming Aeneas Piccolomini and the Regensburg diet on canvases 0-1.

identification: Anonymous, Audi tellus, audi magni maris limbus, trope to the responsory Libera me (AH 49 no. 779), str. 1-6, on Frg. 7-11v and the pasted Adl. piece
note: Frg. 7-11v and the pasted Adl. piece carry strophes 1-6 of the Libera trope Audi tellus, read on the images and compared with AH 49 no. 779, pp. 378-380; an independent research reader read the left block of 7-11v blind on canvas 5 and checked it against the AH page images. The Ubi list (str. 5-6) is expanded and reordered against every arrangement AH prints (adds Ubi fortes, Democritus, Tullius, Aristoteles vir doctissimus, Ubi Salomon sapientissimus) and line 4b is doubled with 'Perit enim rerum maneries'. 'Ubi Sampson ... ubi Absalon' come only from a modern typed slip (which reads 'versucia') and Media vita only from a mirror offset on 7-8v; neither is claimed. The German documentary notes on 7-1v, 7-4v and 7-7v are unread and not identified.

identification: Jacobus de Voragine, Legenda aurea, cap. 168 (Elizabeth: devotion in marriage; the burning young man) and cap. 170 (Clement: the pirates and Justina; Faustinianus and Simon Magus; the apocryphal Itinerarium Clementis), Graesse 1850 pp. 754-755, 762, 781-783
note: Sustained agreement in wording and order with Graesse on four passages, one per page, compared by a research reader on page images of Graesse; the coordinator checked the foot of canvas 0 left ('Dixitque petrus faustino' to 'ut simonem [ma]gum') against the page image of Graesse p. 783. The author's comment on the apocryphal Itinerarium Clementis places the Clement leaf in the Legenda aurea rather than in Rufinus's Recognitiones. Differences are small (e.g. 'maxime' for 'misericordiae', 'faustino' for 'Faustiniano'). The claim covers the passages read: the two Elizabeth pages appear to be back to back yet are about 220 Graesse lines apart, which is unexplained, and the canvas 0 left column stops mid-sentence with the rest of its ruled column blank. Same-codex candidate with F-bwv7 (Frg. 222) on measurements (line spacing about 5.15 mm, column about 149 mm).

identification: Gregory the Great, Moralia in Iob XIX.xxvi.47-xxvii.49 (on Job 29:17-18)
note: Vertically cut leaf, one column, recto line beginnings and verso line ends; four passages from both faces agree in wording and sequence with PL 76 cols. 129-130 (page image), e.g. 'Contra hunc leonem sancta ecclesia ... fidei caulas munit' and 'Palma enim tarde proficit'. A research reader reread every legible line on the images and collated them; the coordinator read about 16 lines at the top of canvas 1 against the PL page image. Differences include promittebat/promittebant, 'Hec immerito uita iustorum'/'Nec immerito justorum vita' and 'Habet quippe'/'Habet quidem'; Odo of Cluny's abridgement lacks phrases present on the leaf. A modern paper slip supplies only the lost ends of two Bible quotations; the critical edition (CCSL 143A) was not consulted.

identification: Peter Lombard, Commentarius in Psalmos, on Ps 104:5-19 and 105:6-22 (PL 191, cols. 948-952, 961-966)
note: Bifolium, two columns, red-underlined lemmata and red marginal source sigla (ag, c) matching PL's [Aug.], [Cassiod.]; a research reader collated one passage from each face with the PL 191 page images (cols. 949-950, 963) and found sustained agreement, with small differences such as a compressed repeated clause, 'per quod' for 'per quem' and no 'hic' in 'Talis locutio est'. Gilbert of Poitiers's Media glosatura, read in Cambridge, Queens' College MS 18 at Ps 104:12 and 104:14-15, lacks passages the fragment shares with Lombard; this rests on one witness and two verses. The coordinator verified on the images that the text runs across the join into F-qslo (Stams Frg. 213), 'si non moy-|-ses electus eius', so the two bifolia are one manuscript, F-bjvu nested inside F-qslo. A machine-read manuscript text search (CoMMA) ranks Lombard manuscripts highest and is supporting only. A typed label records use as the wrapper of Stams VIII/F-37 (Fasciculus temporum 1481 and Glareanus, Liber de asse 1550).

identification: Peter Lombard, Commentarius in Psalmos, Ps 103:29-104:5 and Ps 105:22-43 (PL 191, cols. 941-948, 965-970)
note: A two-column parchment bifolium of Peter Lombard's Psalter commentary, with lemmata underlined in red and marginal source sigla for Augustine and Cassiodorus. A research reader collated five passages from both faces against PL 191 (OCR and page images); wording and sequence agree, including Lombard's own linking phrases. The variants are minor, e.g. 'inficiebant' for 'interficiebant' at Ps 105:37. It is the outer bifolium around F-bjvu (Stams Frg. 187): the text runs on across both joins, and Gilbert of Poitiers was excluded on one witness there. The abraded lower part of face r column d and the parts of face v under a mirror-image offset of another document were not read.

identification: Peter Comestor, Historia scholastica, III Regum cap. 29-37 (PL 198, cols. 1373-1381)
note: Four strips from a two-column manuscript; each strip shows the inner edges of two columns, and both faces read in sequence (strip order 1, 4, 2, 3). A research reader collated four column pieces on strips 1 and 4, both faces, with the PL 198 page images (cols. 1373, 1375, 1377): Comestor's Incidentia on Herodotus and Sesac, the 'Sub Asa fuit' note with Josephus on Creon, the synecdoche note on Abia and Asa, and Jeroboam's withered hand. The coordinator read strip 2, canvas 0, right column on the image against col. 1378 (Elijah at Carith, with Comestor's 'aposiopesis est'). Differences are scribal (Susac, Zela, 'precedebant', 'his annis', 'aliquot' absent, a rubric 'Incidentia' before 'Sub Asa fuit'). Strip 3 rests on the image-only reading; the support (paper per catalogue) and the leaf layout were not examined.

identification: Aristotle, Posterior Analytics, Latin (James of Venice tradition), I.11-12 and II.13-19
note: Nine strips of a glossed manuscript in Gothic bookhand. A research reader reread 36-4r (I.12, 77b1-18), 36-5r (II.16, 98a35-b21) and 36-8r (II.17-19, 99b7-22) on the images and collated them with page images of the Leonine textus (pp. 219, 389, 392-393) and PL 64 (cols. 723-724, 757-760). The coordinator read 36-7r (I.12, 77b16-40, 18 lines) against the Leonine p. 222 page image and PL 64 col. 724. Agreement with the two prints is mixed (on 7r six readings with the Leonine, two with PL, and 'ut in dyalecticis' in neither), and Aristoteles Latinus IV was not available, so James's version versus Moerbeke's revision stays open. 36-6r is placed in II.14 in outline, seven pieces only from the image-only reading, and 36-3v and 36-6v are unplaced; the pencil r/v labels are reversed on piece 4.

identification: Unidentified German devotional prose on worthy reception of the Eucharist, with a section on the nine choirs of angels
note: A folded paper fragment in a 15th-century Bavarian-Austrian cursive with German devotional prose on worthy reception of the Eucharist. It cites the centurion and the royal official's son told as one story, the Emmaus disciples, Oza struck for touching the ark, and 'credo et manduco'. It also contains a section on the nine choirs of angels in Gregory's order, citing Gregory and Dionysius, and on the threefold hierarchy. Phrase searches in Google Books, Internet Archive, MDZ, Corpus Corporum and the Handschriftenportal found no source. One lead remains untested: the 'Traktat über die neun Chöre der Engel' in Berlin, Staatsbibliothek, Ms. germ. oct. 517, f. 24v (15th century, Bavarian), for which no digitisation is listed.

identification: Pseudo-Aristotle, Secretum secretorum, Latin of Philip of Tripoli, end of Part II to Part III (moon and laxatives; herbs and stones prologue; Emerald Tablet; marvellous stones; plants and planets), ed. Steele 1920, pp. 109-120
note: A research reader collated passages from all four columns line by line against Steele's page images (pp. 109, 114-120), finding sustained agreement in wording and sequence with Philip of Tripoli's Latin base text, not Bacon's glosses. A second research reader independently read canvas 0 col. a lines 13-25 (the red and white stones) and found agreement with Steele p. 118 over 13 lines, with 'pondus derham' for 'pondus denarii'. Other version differences: 'planetarum' for 'plantarum' repeatedly, 'philosophando' for 'prophetando', 'luna accrescente' for 'decrescens', the Pliny note on the Moon carried in the text (Steele reports it only as a footnote; compared on OCR), and several eye-skip omissions. Text order runs from canvas 1 (pencil 'v') to canvas 0 (pencil 'r'). A later vertical inscription, 'Vrbarium / Mitlkhellner Ambts, auf das Sechzehen- / hundert dreyzehent Jar', shows the leaf was the cover of the 1613 Urbar of the Mittelkellner office. The lower half of canvas 0 col. b is unread, and the copy is not placed in the manuscript tradition.

identification: Latin medical treatise in numbered chapters (Caroline minuscule); c. xxxiii 'De adipibus'; sources Galen, Methodus medendi XIV.4-5 (Kühn X 956-958) and ps.-Galen, De simplicibus medicamentis ad Paternianum, 'De sepo'
note: The lines before c. xxxiii on the legible face (canvas 1) agree in content and key terms with Galen MM XIV.4-5: the stony hardening, remedies 'medici vocant malactica', and bull, calf and lion fat. This was checked against Kühn's Latin through archive.org OCR, not page images. Chapter xxxiii's ranking of fats follows the ps.-Galenic Ad Paternianum entry 'De sepo' in sequence and phrasing ('melius ... ursinum quam taurinum', 'spissius et siccius et magis hircinum', goose fat best among birds). That comparison used OCR of the Venice 1565 Galen and Google Books snippets of the 1562-1639 editions; I saw no page image. The Ad Glauconem 'Liber tertius' in Einsiedeln, Stiftsbibliothek, Cod. 304 was read on the page images (pp. 70-100, 170-181): it is disease therapy from head to foot with no fats or malactica chapter, so it is excluded as far as it survives. The lost Chartres MS 62 'condensed De methodo medendi', which had a chapter 'De virtutibus adipum', remains an untestable candidate. Canvas 0 (pencil recto) is almost entirely abraded and was not read.

identification: Boniface VIII, Liber Sextus 1.3.10-11 (Friedberg II cols. 941-942), with the Glossa ordinaria of Johannes Andreae on VI 1.3.8, 10 and 11
note: Glossed leaf: main text VI 1.3.10 'Si propter tua debita' and VI 1.3.11 'Statutum' to §3, running from face r column b into face v column a, with line ends of VI 1.3.8-9 on a pasted strip. A research reader collated the main text with the Friedberg II page image (cols. 941-942) and the face v gloss with the page images of the Turin 1588 glossed Sextus (cols. 35-38: Vacabunt, Impediri, Praeiudicium aliquod, Statutum); the coordinator read face v column a lower half against Friedberg col. 941 and 14 lines of the face r upper gloss against 1588 col. 33 (the gloss on VI 1.3.8). Main-text differences unrecorded by Friedberg: no 'in ea', 'docuit experiencia', 'dinoscantur', 'commissionis'; the gloss omits 'translatione', cites 'xlv di.' for the print's '55 dist.' and carries the siglum 'Jo. And.'. The only later writing is a pencil host or shelf note 'V d/M,9 (1548)', not a title. Most of the face r lower gloss and a small adjoining piece remain unplaced; the gloss was compared with one printed edition only.

identification: Terence, Andria, vv. 527-545 (III.2-3) and 738-756 (IV.3-4)
note: A paper bifolium in one early modern cursive hand with drawn scene initials, from the binding of Stams II/G 36 (1534); its four pages carry Andria vv. 527-545 and 738-756 with both scene headings and speaker sigla. A research reader reread all four pages on the native images and collated them with page images of Umpfenbach's edition (1870), pp. 45-46 and 61-62, text and apparatus. The coordinator re-read vv. 531-535 (canvas 1, right page) on the image against pp. 45-46. The variants follow the medieval manuscripts (per ego te D E, ipsus B D1 G, in ipso tempore D G, hem nusquam est D E G); 'Per unicam', 'video', 'Dic clare quod rogo' and 'tun adposisti' are not in Umpfenbach's apparatus. The exemplar, date beyond the binding and the support were not examined.

identification: Jacobus de Voragine, Legenda aurea, cap. 168 (Elizabeth, end: posthumous miracles) and cap. 169 (Cecilia: etymology; Valerian and Almachius), Graesse 1850 pp. 770-771, 774-776
note: Sustained agreement in wording and order with Graesse on two passages, one per page: Elizabeth's miracles with the Cecilia etymology (right page, lines 9-31) and the Valerian-Almachius dialogue (left page, lines 1-23), compared by a research reader on page images of Graesse; the coordinator checked 14 lines of the left page against the page image of Graesse p. 775. Variants include the absent Scintrudis miracle, no name for the woman of Trier, a different ending to the Mechtildis miracle, and 'interitum' for 'luctum'. The other face is under paper, and the bifolium is probably the central one of its gathering. Same-codex candidate with F-rdns (Frg. 122) on measurements (line spacing about 5.2 mm, column about 149 mm); not shown to share a codex with F-n2rx (Frg. 219), which is ruled differently.

identification: Rhymed offices of St Kunigunde (end of Matins to Second Vespers; AH 26 no. 77) and of the Canonization of St Henry II ('In festo Canonizationis sancti Heinrici imperatoris', First Vespers to Matins nocturn III, R. Aeterna tactus; Bamberg breviary 1575, pp. 745-750)
note: Two consecutive paper leaves of an office book without lessons, text order 107-2v, 2r, 1v, 1r (the pencilled r/v labels are reversed on both leaves; the join was confirmed by two readers). A research reader compared the Henry chants, chapter, hymn cue and collect with the Bamberg breviary of 1575 and the Kunigunde chants with Analecta Hymnica 26 on page images, finding sustained agreement in wording and order; a second research reader read the Lauds antiphons and the 1v join before seeing a source and confirmed it. Variants include germine (1575 gemine), expertus (experitur), copulat/consignat (copulavit/consignavit), and against AH quia, comprobat, humilitatis, commendat, 'Nos solve nexu'. The psalm scheme is secular, not monastic or Cistercian; the diocese of use (Bamberg-like, but the office was also used in Augsburg, Salzburg and Austria) is not established, and date and origin were not assessed.

identification: Office of the Crown of Thorns (De spinea corona), Matins, monastic arrangement, from the chapter Egredimini to the nocturn III homily; lessons from Chrysostom, In Ioh. hom. 84 (medieval Latin), Bernard, Sermo in feria IV Hebdomadae sanctae 8-9, and Augustine, In Ioh. tract. 116
note: One parchment leaf of a monastic breviary, later a binding wrapper. A research reader compared the chants with the Cantus Database transcription of the Cistercian antiphoner of Rein (A-Wn Cod. 1799**, ff. 228r-231r), the only inventory with the whole run of fifteen chants in this order, and the chants, rubrics and lessons with the Historia de spinea corona (Dillingen 1584) on page images; a second research reader read canvas 0 column b lines 11-22 before opening the print and confirmed sustained agreement. The leaf matches neither witness exactly: its nocturn II psalm cues for antiphons 5-6 (Domine Deus salutis, Dominus regnavit) differ from both Rein and the print (Te decet, Domine Deus salutis), its nocturn III versicle agrees with the print against Rein, and its lesson division differs from the print's (split at Propterea and Tu vero, print Lectio IIII Si contumeliam absent, two lessons not in the print). Cistercian use is an inference only; date, origin and the source of lesson viii are not established.

identification: Noted breviary, use not established: Good Friday Matins nocturn III (Heb 6:8-7:5; R. Iesum tradidit, R. Caligaverunt), Lauds, Vespers and Compline rubrics, Holy Saturday Matins nocturn I (In pace, Habitabit, Caro mea; Lam 3:22-66, R. Sicut ovis; Lam 4, R. Jerusalem luge); rubrics agree with the Ordinal of Innocent III (Van Dijk 1975, pp. 244, 259-260)
note: The run of lessons, chants and rubrics was read on all four pages and agrees in content and order with the papal-court Ordinal of Innocent III (Van Dijk and Walker 1975, pp. 244, 259-260), compared in Google Books snippets only; the nine-responsory structure is that of the secular cursus, but monastic books also used it on these days, so the use is not established. An independent research reader read Lam 4:4-14 (canvas 1 col 1) on the image against the Vulgate. The leaf has 'sine capitulo' (with a Franciscan breviary rubric) for the Ordinal's 'sine lectione', and omits filiae, mulierum and sacerdotum in Lam 4. Which book of the curial/Franciscan/Roman-use family it came from, its date and origin, and the extent of the Good Friday nocturn III lessons are not established.

identification: Noted hymnal, probably Cistercian: Common of Saints (end of Deus tuorum militum, Iesu corona virginum, Christe cunctorum) and hymns of an Office of the Passion, probably of the Crown of Thorns (end of Bonaventure's Christum ducem; Beata Christi passio with Qui pressura in the arrangement of Mone's MS K; Iesu velatus facie at Terce); Mone I nos. 85-87
note: The hymns were read on all four pages and compared with Mone, Lateinische Hymnen I nos. 84-91 (archive.org OCR text) and with Waddell's Primitive Cistercian Breviary (Google Books snippets); an independent research reader read canvas 1 left against Waddell and Cantus and found agreement apart from 'adque' and 'mentibus' (Waddell 'atque', 'sensibus'). Qui pressura agrees with every feature Mone reports for his Karlsruhe MS K, headed for the feast of the Crown of Thorns, and Iesu velatus facie is listed under De corona spinea in Clm 2541 (at Terce) and Heidelberg Cod. Sal. X,7 (Salem) in MMMO; the leaf itself has no feast heading, so the occasion is probable. The Deus tuorum militum ending, the division of Iesu corona virginum and the Gloria tibi domine doxology make Cistercian use probable. The marginal rubric on canvas 1 right is unread, the leaf order is not settled, and the date and origin were not examined.

identification: Deed of sale: Abbot Pelagius of Stams, with the consent of King Ferdinand I, sells Ludwig von Brunnenstain a redeemable yearly rent on pledged abbey woods, tithes and rights (redemption 300 gulden); Michaelmas (29 September), probably [1539] (1538 not excluded), place lost
note: The regest is read on the image: issuer Abbot P(?)elagius of Stams (first letters uncertain, ending -agius clear), the Roman king's consent, buyer Ludwig von Brunnenstain, sale of a redeemable rent on pledged abbey property, redemption at 300 gulden with return of the letter, and the dating clause 'sannt Michels des heiligen Ertzenngels tag' (29 September). The year is lost at the cut right edge and is supplied as [1539]: the text names 1539 in line 7, and Pelagius Baur resigned on 18 April 1540 (Monasticon metropolis Salzburgensis, 1908, snippet); if line 7's 1539 is a future payment date, 1538 is possible. A fresh reader given neutral crops confirmed the year words of line 7, the Michaelmas clause, 'Ludwigen von Brunnenstain' and the back title 'Ad Annum 15.77'; it saw only '?reagius' for the abbot, which the coordinator reread as Pelagius. The capital, the yearly rent, the place and the buyer's identity are not established; no outside record of the act was found (monasterium.net Stams regests, ÖStA, Regesta Imperii, Google Books searched).

identification: Lehenbrief of King Ferdinand I as count of Tyrol: Hans Veit von Annenberg, for himself and as Lehenträger for Anthoni, Sigmund and Jacob, after the death of [...]ristan von Annenberg, receives the Tyrolean fiefs (castle at Latsch with orchard, sawmill, tithes, meadows, farms), with confirmation of a grace of King Henry; [1527-1564] by title, dating clause lost
note: The regest is read on the image: the royal style ('...Hungern, Behaim, Dalmatien, Croatien etc. Künig, Infant', which in a grant of Tyrolean fiefs fits only Ferdinand I), Hans Veit von Annenberg as petitioner for himself and as Lehenträger for Anthoni, Sigmund and Jacob, the grant of the fiefs of the County of Tyrol after the death of '[...]ristan von Annenberg', the confirmation of King Henry's grace, and the fief list beginning with the castle at Latsch. The left part of every line and the dating clause are cut away; the date is [1527-1564] from the title alone. A fresh reader given neutral crops confirmed the style, the names, 'Künig Hainrichs', 'Burg zu L(a/o)tsch' and the back title '15 Stambs 64', and with the coordinator read '[...]ristan' in line 4, correcting a proposed '[Ch]ristof' and withdrawing a narrower date. The surname's minims allow Ammenberg; Annenberg rests on the fief group, which matches the 1510 Annenberg Lehensrevers quoted in the Hofnamen im Landgericht Schlanders (snippets) in items, order and wording. No record of this act was found; sealing cannot be checked.

identification: Two documents of Bishop Georg of Austria of Brixen (1525-1539) to the parish clergy of his city and diocese: (A) annual circular on the cathedraticum, examination of curates, alms collectors and reserved and marriage cases, with the calendar of movable feasts for 1530; (B) faculty for Lenten confessions with reserved cases; issued [1529], no dating clause, copy on paper
note: The leaf holds two documents, each opening 'Georgius dei gratia Episcopus Brixinensis'; issuer, addressees and substance of both are read on the image. Neither keeps a dating clause: the circular's calendar is for 'Anno Tricesimo proximo venturo', and its figures (letter B, Septuagesima 13 February, Easter 17 April, Pentecost 5 June, Corpus Christi 16 June) fit 1530 (Julian), so it was issued in [1529]; Georg was bishop 1525-1538/39 (snippets). A fresh reader given neutral crops confirmed both openings, letter B, the Septuagesima and Easter dates and 'Quade[ragesima]'; it read 'Tricesimo primo', which the coordinator reread as 'Tricesimo proximo uenturo' (x clear), and the calendar fits 1530, not 1531. The unsealed paper leaf is a copy or chancery exemplar, later the cover of Stams item II/633 (1535); place and day of issue are lost. No outside record of either circular was found.

identification: Deed of sale: Abbot [Bernhard] and the convent of Stams sell Hans V[eh]lin and Anton Welser of [Memmingen] a redeemable yearly rent of 50 Malter rye from the abbey's great corn tithe at Kettershausen (Augsburg diocese) for 1100 Rhenish gulden; Friday after St George, probably [14]92 (27 April 1492); cancelled original in two strips
note: The two strips are one charter, each line running from item 1 on into item 2. Issuer, buyers, object, place, 50 Malter (25 each), price 'ailffhundert' gulden, payment between Martinmas and Christmas, redemption, sealing and the dating clause 'In dem Zwa[y]vnd ne[w]ntzigisten Jare An freytag nach sant Jörgen' are read; the abbot's name and the hundreds of the year are lost at the left edge and supplied, and the unit 'Zwa[y]' is uncertain. Hans Vöhlin died on 18 March 1496 (snippets), which excludes 1496 and fixes 27 April 1492; Abbot Bernhard of Stams is attested in 1492 (monasterium.net regests). A fresh reader given neutral crops confirmed the issuer, Anton Welser, 50 Malter, Augsburg diocese on the Günz, Kettershausen, the seal clause, the St George clause and the endorsement; it lost the year's tens under holes, could not read the sums and read the first buyer's faded surname otherwise; the coordinator reread the year as above, the sums as 'ailffhundert' and the surname as V[eh]lin, and the third person's forename, [Er?]hard or Bernhard Vöhlin of Memmingen, keeps its first letters lost. No outside record of the sale was found.
